title: T-6: per-set Playwright feature project + test:features:all (both sets, one server) as the E2E co-residency proof
recipe: src/server/app/docs/add-a-set.md STEP 7 (test scaffolding — the per-set Playwright project) with SIBLING-SET-PLAN.md §7 T-6 as REVISED 2026-08-01 by ruling R3 supplying the detail. Note the plan section changed substantively: with one server serving both sets, the plant project is not a different SERVER, only a different testDir and baseURL path-space.

filesToTouch.what: Two edits, both small. (1) Append a new project object to the existing `projects` array, after the `features` project (lines 42-52), copying its `use` block exactly: { name: 'features-plant-products', testDir: './src/server/app/sets/plant-products/journeys/linear/features', testMatch: '**/*.e2e.spec.js', use: { ...devices['Desktop Chrome'], baseURL: `http://localhost:${port}`, video: 'off', trace: 'retain-on-failure' } }. Do NOT touch the `journeys` or `features` projects — `features` is ALREADY live-animals-scoped by its own testDir, so it needs no change and its specs keep navigating to root-mounted URLs. Plant specs navigate to /plant-products/… ; the baseURL is the same host for both, because it is the same server. (2) ONE edit to the shared `webServer` block (lines 54-63): add `PLANT_PRODUCTS_MODE: 'stub'` to its `env` object alongside the existing `LIVE_ANIMALS_MODE: 'stub'`. Both sets then run on their own stubs in the self-hosted server and the two projects can share ONE server process. `reuseExistingServer: false` stays. Do NOT add an explanatory comment about env merging — the round-1 plan mandated one because SERVED_SET had to be smuggled through Playwright's env merge; ruling R3 deleted that variable, so the subtlety no longer exists and the comment would be stale the day it is written.

Two scripts, added beside the existing test:features (line 21) and mirroring its exact shape (build:frontend prefix + DEMO_SLOWMO/DEMO_PACE_MS vars — build config is load-bearing; without build:frontend the self-hosted app 404s its bundles). (1) "test:features:plant-products": "npm run build:frontend && PLANT_PRODUCTS_MODE=stub DEMO_SLOWMO=0 DEMO_PACE_MS=0 playwright test --project=features-plant-products" — PLANT_PRODUCTS_MODE is the ONLY env var, and it selects the plant RECORDS STUB; it does not select a set. There is NO SERVED_SET. (2) "test:features:all": "npm run build:frontend && DEMO_SLOWMO=0 DEMO_PACE_MS=0 playwright test --project=features --project=features-plant-products" — both projects in ONE invocation against ONE webServer. This is the E2E-level counterpart to co-residency.test.js and the standing proof that both sets serve correctly from the same running process. test:features itself is untouched.

CONDITIONAL — only if none of the three pp-007 m0 specs already asserts content unique to the plant set: strengthen one existing assertion to target plant-set-only rendered copy, so a page served by live-animals could not satisfy it. Under co-residency this is no longer an env-pass-through proof (there is no env to pass through) — it is a MOUNT proof: it pins that /plant-products/… is served by the plant gateway and not accidentally by a live-animals route. No new test cases; no change if the assertion already exists.

CONDITIONAL — only if pp-007's spec does not already do it: keep/add the assertion that GET '/' in the SAME run still serves the live-animals dashboard while GET '/plant-products' serves the plant one. The dashboard is the page where the two sets would collide first (both would claim '/' without the mount prefix), so this is the cheapest E2E co-residency canary and it belongs in the suite that test:features:all runs.

notes: AMENDED 2026-08-01 for Sam's ruling R3 (co-residency) — RETITLED, because half the round-1 title described a problem that no longer exists. 'webServer env pass-through' was the mechanism for smuggling SERVED_SET through Playwright's env merge into the self-hosted server; the reversal deletes SERVED_SET, so there is nothing to pass through and the carefully-worded config comment the round-1 plan mandated is dropped rather than written (a comment recording a subtlety that no longer exists is worse than none). WHAT REPLACES IT: (a) the new features-plant-products project, whose specs navigate to /plant-products/… while live-animals specs are UNEDITED and keep navigating to root-mounted URLs — the two projects differ only by testDir and path-space, not by server; (b) test:features:plant-products carrying PLANT_PRODUCTS_MODE=stub ONLY, which selects the plant RECORDS STUB and emphatically does not select a set; (c) ONE edit to the shared webServer env block adding PLANT_PRODUCTS_MODE: 'stub' beside LIVE_ANIMALS_MODE: 'stub', so both sets run on their stubs in the same self-hosted process; (d) NEW — test:features:all, running both projects in a single invocation against a single server. (d) is the point of the whole increment: it is the E2E-level counterpart to co-residency.test.js and the thing the pre-reversal plan had no way to express, because two sets could not be served at once. It joins the standing verification ladder for every platform-touching increment from here on. The round-1 corrections still hold: the existing `features` project is ALREADY live-animals-scoped via its testDir (playwright.config.js:43-45), so scoping it was a no-op and it stays untouched; and the plan's literal script text omits the build:frontend prefix and DEMO_SLOWMO/DEMO_PACE_MS vars that every existing Playwright script carries, so the scripts here mirror test:features' full shape (missing build:frontend would 404 the bundles silently). The test:e2e whole-journey plant split remains pp-041 (m4), and it too becomes a testDir/baseURL-path split rather than a second server. Exemplars: the existing `features` project block and the test:features script are the idiom — copy, do not invent. Baseline guard: run test:live-animals and PORT=3050 test:features BEFORE editing; red baseline = stop and report.
openQuestions: Exact filenames of the pp-007 dashboard/hub e2e specs are set by pp-007's build (assumed features/dashboard/dashboard.e2e.spec.js and features/hub/hub.e2e.spec.js per the co-location convention) — confirm the actual paths on disk before wiring assertions; the new project's glob picks them up regardless of name.

Running both projects against one webServer means the two sets share a process and therefore share nothing but must not interfere. If test:features:all is flaky while each project passes alone, that is a co-residency defect (most likely ALS context bleed or shared stub state), NOT test flakiness to be retried away — stop and raise it against the co-residency mechanism.
